name: first-principles
description: Coding discipline as seven independent gates rather than a workflow, over a shared canon: verified beats assumed; one state, one owner; fix the class not the instance; change exactly what was asked (changing correct code is worse than leaving a suspicion unfixed); reversibility decides who acts — plus a six-rule security spine. scope-gate agrees on observable done before code. build-gate holds edit discipline, the producer/consumer audit, and falsification of a handed-down finding before it is implemented. cut-gate removes agent-written bloat from a change that already works, against a 47-shape catalog tiered by blast radius — clearing the mocked-out tests and swallowed errors that make every later check unreadable before touching structure, and deciding whether each test earns its keep by whether it can fail on a real defect and survive a correct refactor; it is the one gate that edits rather than reports, logging every finding first and closing red if any is left undisposed. done-gate runs five verification layers including an adversarial pass and a reachability trace. bug-gate debugs and audits against an eighteen-shape bug catalog, tiering findings as proven / traced / suspected. ship-gate handles secrets, config risk, and human-gated irreversibles. watch-gate asks whether a failure would ever be noticed. adversarial-delegation supplies the mechanics for running a gate over a delegated worker you review rather than trust. Each gate produces a verdict with evidence and admits its gaps.
